rfm_tuples.R: 10-K (filed 2025-02-28): 'Dividends declared during the year ended December 31, 2024 of $0.82 per share, representing a 5.8% year-over-year increase. ... We intend to continue to declare quarterly distributions.' Q4 2024 dividend = $0.205/share (run-rate $0.82/yr).
rfm_tuples.f: claim_evolution: compare 10-K dividend forward-looking language (Feb 28) to pre-cutoff 10-Q dividend declarations (filed May 9 for Q1 2025). Look for any cadence change declared between filings.
rfm_tuples.M_source: edgar pre-cutoff 10-Q (0001569187-25-000070), Note on Dividends and Distributions
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 dividend declared March 12, 2025 = $0.140/share (paid April 3, 2025) — 31.7% cut vs $0.205/share Q4 2024 run-rate. Declared just 12 days after the 10-K was filed. The 10-K never warned of an imminent cut; it explicitly framed FY2024 dividend as 'representing a 5.8% year-over-year increase' and signaled intent to 'continue to declare quarterly distributions.'
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Highest-severity claim-evolution finding. The 10-K's framing of dividend trajectory (positive YoY, continuing quarterly cadence) is contradicted within 12 days by a 31.7% cut. While the 10-K language is technically conditional ('intend to' / 'will depend on factors'), the absence of any forward-looking caution in a filing that close in time to the cut indicates either (a) the board had not yet decided, OR (b) the decision was known and concealed. Either reading is a Mode-A failure of disclosure-discipline. The new CEO Tibbetts (effective Jan 1, 2025) likely drove the cut as a post-succession reset; the timing makes it materially worse than a normal Q1 reset because it post-dates the 10-K.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Item 1A risk factor: 'fluctuations in interest rates' listed as a generic risk. Item 7A interest rate derivatives table discloses $1.186B of swap notional. Risk factor narrative does not quantify the volume of debt with swap expirations in 2025 vs the volume with hedges extending into 2026+.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — given the claim that AHH manages interest rate risk via swaps, derive: how much of the swap notional rolls off within 12 months of the filing? Cross-check disclosed swap table.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Of $1.186B total swap notional at 12/31/24, $820M (69%) expires Oct-Dec 2025 (Harbor Point Parcel 3 $90M 10/2025; floating pool $330M 10/2025; Harbor Point Parcel 4 $100M 11/2025; floating pool $300M 12/2025). Only $366M of hedges extend beyond 2025. Q1 2025 added a $150M swap @ 2.50% expiring Jan 2027 (paid $4.6M premium = ~3.1% upfront). Implied cost to replace the full $820M at similar pricing ~ $25M of upfront premium; alternatively, allowing roll-off at SOFR 4.32% (vs blended swap fixed of ~2.75-3.50%) implies ~$30-40M of incremental annual interest expense post-rolloff.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosed in the table but not headlined in narrative. Mode-B framework Q: a REIT with $820M of swaps expiring in a single 90-day window represents a cliff-risk that materially exceeds the diffuse risk-factor language. The $4.6M premium paid for one $150M Jan-2025 swap is the price discovery point. The 10-K does not quantify or even structurally call out this rolloff. Heuristic: hedge-rolloff disclosure quality is a strong Mode-B signal for floating-rate-heavy REITs.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note 19: 'A group of three construction customers comprised 78%, 94%, and 89% of the Company's general contracting and real estate services revenues for the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively. These three construction customers comprised 19%, 18%, and 10% of the Company's total revenues for the year ended December 31, 2024 ...'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify whether the 3-customer concentration is acknowledged as a key risk. Mode B — derive: if GC backlog were to decline, does the filing quantify the run-off risk to consolidated revenue?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 19 (concentrations); 10-K Item 1A; Q1 2025 10-Q construction backlog disclosure
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K: GC backlog $123.8M at 12/31/24, with gross profit $13.9M for FY2024. Item 1A discusses construction-segment customer concentration generically ('our failure to generate income in our general contracting and real estate services segment in amounts that we anticipate') but does NOT name the 3 customers, the dollar exposure per customer, or the contract end-dates. Q1 2025 10-Q: backlog fell to $80.4M (-35% QoQ), GC revenue fell from $127M (Q1 2024) to $46.6M (Q1 2025, -63%), GC gross profit fell to $1.4M (vs $13.9M FY2024 — implies <$6M annualized).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B finding. The 10-K disclosed customer-concentration percentages but did not (a) name the customers, (b) provide backlog by customer, (c) flag that the largest customer's pipeline was running off. The Q1 2025 result (revenue -41% YoY, GC -63%, backlog -35% QoQ) confirms that the GC segment was in active wind-down at year-end but the 10-K narrative did not signal it. For a diversified REIT marketed as having a recurring GC fee stream, the silent collapse of an $80M revenue stream is the kind of disclosure gap that Heuristic 7 (counterparty disclosure mirror) targets. Without customer names, EDGAR FTS cross-check cannot be run.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: 'As of December 31, 2024, we had approximately $121.4 million in outstanding real estate financing investments [mezzanine loans / preferred equity in development JVs]. These types of investments involve a higher degree of risk than long-term senior mortgage loans ... because the investment may become unsecured as a result of foreclosure by the senior lender.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — verify whether any of the mezzanine investments showed signs of borrower distress (preference-rate amendments, extensions, modifications) between 10-K filing date (Feb 28) and 10-Q filing date (May 9).
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-Q Note 7 (Notes Receivable / Real Estate Financing Investments)
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-Q discloses: Solis Gainesville II preference rate REDUCED from 10% to 6% effective Jan 1, 2025 (40% yield cut on one mezz position). 10-K text does NOT disclose this amendment despite being effective ~2 months before the 10-K filing. AHH also received a call option to purchase a controlling interest at FMV during 2025 — i.e., the borrower's economics were impaired enough that the equity option had to be given up to keep the loan performing.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-A failure. A 40% yield cut on a material real-estate-financing position effective Jan 1, 2025 should have been disclosed in the FY2024 10-K (filed Feb 28, 2025) as a subsequent event under ASC 855. The Solis Gainesville II amendment is omitted from the 10-K but appears in the 10-Q ~10 weeks later. Small dollar in isolation but a credible canary for the broader $121M mezz book — when one borrower has to renegotiate the preference rate down by 40%, other Solis-sponsor positions (Terwilliger Pappas has 5 of the active mezz loans) are likely under similar stress. The 10-K characterizes the mezz portfolio as a distinguishing competitive strength rather than a stressed asset class.

rfm_tuples.f: claim_evolution / FFO-quality: compare reported FFO trend vs Normalized FFO trend; check for FFO-padding via derivative MTM.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY2024: FFO $99.8M ($1.08/sh) vs Normalized FFO $118.9M ($1.29/sh) — $19.1M gap. Q1 2025: FFO $17.2M ($0.17/sh) vs Normalized FFO $25.6M ($0.25/sh). Q1 2024: FFO $35.0M ($0.40/sh) vs Normalized FFO $29.4M ($0.33/sh). Translation: in Q1 2024 FFO > Normalized (derivative gains FLATTERED FFO); in Q1 2025 Normalized FFO > FFO (derivative LOSSES of $5.6M MTM are scrubbed in the Normalized number). The reversal is concealed by the Normalized FFO framing — the underlying recurring earnings power declined from $0.33 to $0.25 (-24%) on the cleaner Normalized basis, and from $0.40 to $0.17 (-58%) on the GAAP-adjacent FFO basis.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: MODE. The Normalized FFO framing is technically defensible (it scrubs MTM noise both ways) but functionally serves to muffle the deteriorating earnings trajectory. Q1 2025 Normalized FFO of $0.25 vs $0.205 prior quarterly dividend means dividend coverage on Normalized FFO was 0.82x (the dividend cut makes economic sense). The 10-K's emphasis on the $1.29 Normalized FFO without explicit forward guidance on the swap rolloff impact (see C2) is a Mode-B underdelivery on FFO-quality discipline.

Mode-B gap: no top-tenant table (most peer diversified REITs disclose top-10 tenants with % of ABR). The Boykin/HII directorship adjacency is interesting Mode-B color but not load-bearing.

summary: AHH FY2024 10-K + Q1 2025 10-Q: 10 R/f/M claims scored. Severity counts: PASS=3, MODE=3, SEVERE=3, RED=1. Dominant finding is a CLAIM-EVOLUTION RED — the 10-K (filed Feb 28) framed 2024 dividends as a '5.8% year-over-year increase' with forward language saying 'intend to continue to declare quarterly distributions'; just 12 days later on Mar 12, new CEO Tibbetts cut the quarterly dividend 31.7% from $0.205 to $0.140 per share. Three SEVEREs reinforce the disclosure-gap pattern: (a) $820M (69%) of interest-rate swaps roll off Oct-Dec 2025 with no narrative quantification of the rate-reset impact on 2026 FFO; (b) the Solis Gainesville II mezz position had its preference rate cut from 10% to 6% effective Jan 1, 2025, omitted from the 10-K's subsequent events note but appearing in the Q1 10-Q (borderline ASC 855 non-compliance, canary for the $121M mezz book); (c) the general contracting segment is silently winding down (backlog -35% QoQ to $80.4M, GC revenue -63% YoY, gross profit run-rate cratering) with no segment-level forward warning. Counter-weighting: Big-4 auditor with 13-year tenure (PASS), clean covenant compliance (PASS), and crucially — insider behavior is supportive: directors put $2.2M of personal capital into the Sept-2024 offering at $10.50 AND continued to add post-dividend cut at $7.70 (PASS, the load-bearing honesty-alpha CREDIT signal). Verdict: NEUTRAL — the filing has material Mode-A claim-evolution failures on dividend cadence and Mode-B disclosure gaps on swap rolloff + mezz portfolio stress + GC segment runoff, but the insider-pulse is supportive and the auditor + maturity ladder do not signal fraud or imminent distress. Forward -3.5% return (relatively benign) is consistent with NEUTRAL framing rather than SHORT-tier.
framework_notes: Mode A failure: 10-K dividend language (Feb 28) vs Mar 12 dividend cut declaration — the 12-day claim-evolution gap is the strongest single signal. Future m-source: dividend declarations dated within 30 days of a 10-K should auto-cross-check the 10-K's forward language.

Mode B finding: hedge-rolloff cliff disclosure quality — $820M of swaps expiring in 90 days (Oct-Dec 2025) is buried in the swap table without narrative quantification of the rate-reset impact on 2026 FFO. Process rule candidate: m-source connector that flags REITs/yieldcos with >50% of swap notional expiring within 12 months of filing date.

Honesty-alpha CREDIT signal: insider participation in the Sept-2024 offering at $10.50 ($2.2M of director personal capital) followed by additional director buying post-dividend-cut at $7.70 is the cleanest counter-evidence that prevents this name from rising to SHORT-tier. The market priced in the dividend cut (stock $7.17 at cutoff vs $8.91 on Feb 21) but insiders are accumulating, suggesting management believes the cut is a one-time reset.

Subsequent-events disclosure-discipline gap: Solis Gainesville II preference-rate amendment effective Jan 1, 2025 (10-K filed Feb 28) was not disclosed in 10-K but appears in Q1 10-Q (May 9). This is borderline ASC 855 non-compliance and worth tracking as a Mode-B counter-check pattern for any name with disclosed mezzanine / preferred-equity investment book.

Verdict-calibration: this is NEUTRAL with a clear dividend cut and meaningful Mode-B gaps. The framework correctly identifies the disclosure-discipline failure on the dividend but the insider-pulse PASS prevents over-shorting. Forward -3.5% return validates the NEUTRAL call — a fraud-flagged name should have dropped 30%+, while this name dropped just enough to reflect the dividend yield re-rating.
